domains.name: treatment
domains.description: Authoritative domain for all water treatment and purification operations at WTPs and WWTPs. Owns process data for coagulation, filtration, disinfection (UV, chlorination, RO, UF, MF, GAC), CT compliance, chemical dosing, and finished water production. Integrates with SCADA/OSIsoft PI Historian for real-time process control and MOR regulatory submissions.

products.name: facility
products.description: Water treatment plant or facility master record. Stores facility-level attributes including design capacity, treatment technology, regulatory identifiers (PWSID), SCADA integration points, operator certification requirements, and AWIA risk assessment dates. Central entity for treatment operations, compliance reporting (MOR/DMR), and asset management integration (Maximo location). References EPA SDWA, AWIA Section 2013.
products.reference: EPA SDWA 40 CFR 141, AWIA Section 2013, AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs, IBM Maximo Asset Management, OSIsoft PI System

products.name: process_unit
products.description: Individual treatment process unit within a facility (filter, clarifier, membrane train, UV reactor, contact basin). Stores unit-specific design parameters (capacity, media type, surface area, hydraulic loading rate, detention time, baffling factor), operational status, and asset identifiers (Maximo asset number). Used for process control, performance monitoring, and maintenance scheduling.
products.reference: AWWA Water Treatment Plant Design, Ten States Standards, Maximo Asset Hierarchy, PI AF Element Templates

products.name: service_application
products.description: Record of a customer's application to establish, transfer, or modify water and/or wastewater service. Captures application number, application type (new service, transfer, upgrade, downgrade, termination), applicant identity, requested service address, requested service start date, application submission channel (online, phone, walk-in), application status (submitted, under review, approved, rejected, withdrawn), identity verification outcome, credit check result, deposit requirement, and processing timestamps. Represents the start of the customer lifecycle. Sourced from Oracle CC&B and Microsoft Dynamics 365.

products.name: interaction
products.description: Unified record of every customer-initiated or utility-initiated interaction, contact, and account note across all channels — inbound calls, outbound calls, web portal sessions, chat, email, walk-in visits, IVR self-service, and system-generated notes. Captures interaction date and time, channel, interaction type (billing inquiry, service request, complaint, outage report, payment arrangement, general inquiry, staff note, system alert), record subtype (structured interaction vs free-text note), duration, agent ID, note text (for unstructured entries), note visibility level (internal/external), resolution status, case or work order reference, workflow trigger flag, and customer satisfaction score if captured. Sourced from Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM and Oracle CC&B. SSOT for all customer contact history and account annotations. Supports customer service continuity, dispute resolution, and field crew awareness (e.g., dangerous dog, locked gate, medical equipment dependency).

products.name: complaint
products.description: Formal record of a customer complaint or grievance filed with the utility, including water quality complaints, billing disputes, service interruption complaints, pressure complaints, odor/taste complaints, and regulatory complaints escalated to the state primacy agency or PUC. Captures complaint number, complaint category, complaint description, reported date, assigned resolution owner, target resolution date, actual resolution date, resolution description, regulatory escalation flag, and customer satisfaction outcome. Distinct from customer_interaction (which captures all contacts) — a complaint has its own formal resolution workflow and regulatory reporting obligations. [SSOT: Canonical source of truth for this concept across domains.] SSOT master for complaints.

attributes.name: category

Billing disputes cover charges, meter reads, and rate application. Service interruption includes planned and unplanned outages. Pressure issues cover low or high Pounds per Square Inch (PSI). Regulatory complaints are those escalated to state primacy agencies or Public Utilities Commission (PUC). attributes.name: compensation_provided_flag

attributes.name: complaint_number

attributes.name: complaint_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the complaint in the resolution workflow. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: open|in_progress|pending_customer|pending_investigation|resolved|closed|escalated|withdrawn — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]. Ref: AWWA.

attributes.name: contact_method

attributes.name: corrective_action
attributes.description: Specific corrective action taken to address the root cause and prevent recurrence, such as infrastructure repair, meter replacement, billing adjustment, or process improvement. Ref: AWWA.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when the complaint record was first created in the database. Ref: AWWA.

attributes.name: customer_satisfaction_comments

attributes.name: customer_satisfaction_rating

attributes.name: description

attributes.name: follow_up_date

attributes.name: follow_up_required_flag

attributes.name: internal_notes

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when the complaint record was last updated. Ref: AWWA.

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Urgency classification of the complaint based on health and safety risk, regulatory exposure, and customer impact. Critical includes Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL) exceedances and Sanitary Sewer Overflow (SSO) events. Ref: AWWA.

attributes.name: regulatory_agency

attributes.name: regulatory_case_number
attributes.description: Case or reference number assigned by the regulatory agency for tracking the escalated complaint. Ref: AWWA.

attributes.name: regulatory_escalation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the complaint was escalated to or originated from a regulatory agency such as state primacy agency, Public Utilities Commission (PUC), or U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). Ref: AWWA.

attributes.name: regulatory_response_due_date
attributes.description: Date by which the utility must provide a formal response to the regulatory agency regarding the escalated complaint. Ref: AWWA.

attributes.name: reported_date
attributes.description: Date when the complaint was first reported to the utility by the customer. Ref: AWWA.

attributes.name: reported_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the complaint was logged into the system, including time zone offset. Ref: AWWA.

attributes.name: resolution_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative of the actions taken to resolve the complaint, including investigation findings, corrective actions, and customer communication. Ref: AWWA.

attributes.name: resolution_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the complaint was marked as resolved, including time zone offset. Ref: AWWA.

attributes.name: root_cause
attributes.description: Identified root cause of the complaint issue, such as main break, meter malfunction, billing system error, water treatment process deviation, or customer misunderstanding. Ref: AWWA.

attributes.name: ssot_role
attributes.description: SSOT cross-domain reconciliation link. Ref: AWWA.

attributes.name: subcategory
attributes.description: Detailed subcategory providing additional classification granularity within the primary complaint category. Examples: discoloration, chlorine_odor, high_bill, estimated_read, low_pressure, no_water, meter_leak, service_attitude. Ref: AWWA.

attributes.name: target_resolution_date
attributes.description: Target date by which the complaint should be resolved, based on Service Level Agreement (SLA) commitments and regulatory requirements. Ref: AWWA.

attributes.name: water_quality_test_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a water quality test was required or performed as part of the complaint investigation, particularly for complaints involving taste, odor, discoloration, or suspected contamination. Ref: AWWA.

domains.name: distribution
domains.description: Owns the potable water distribution network topology, hydraulic modeling, and operational data including mains, service lines, valves, PRVs, hydrants, pump stations, storage tanks, DMAs, and pressure zones. Integrates with Esri ArcGIS and Innovyze InfoWater for network modeling, NRW/UFW analysis, and pressure (PSI) and flow (GPM/MGD) management.

products.name: pipe_main
products.description: Water distribution main pipes forming the backbone of the distribution network. Tracks material, diameter, length, installation date, condition, break history, and hydraulic characteristics per AWWA M11 Steel Pipe Design and Installation and AWWA C600 Installation of Ductile-Iron Mains. Critical for hydraulic modeling (InfoWater, WaterGEMS), asset management (IBM Maximo), and capital planning. Supports LCRR lead service line inventory requirements and main replacement prioritization.
products.reference: AWWA M11, AWWA C600, EPA LCRR, ISO 24516-1:2016 Asset Management

products.name: pressure_zone
products.description: Hydraulic pressure zones within the distribution system, each maintained at target pressure ranges through storage tanks, pump stations, and PRV stations. Tracks elevation ranges, design pressures, customer count, demand patterns, storage capacity, and NRW metrics. Essential for hydraulic modeling, fire flow analysis, and system planning per AWWA M31 Distribution System Requirements for Fire Protection.
products.reference: AWWA M31, AWWA M32 Distribution Network Analysis, ISO 24516-1:2016

attributes.name: pressure_zone_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the pressure zone within the distribution network. Primary key. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: serving_facility_id

attributes.description: Corresponding feature identifier in the Esri ArcGIS Geographic Information System (GIS) for spatial representation and network topology management. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: average_daily_demand_mgd
attributes.description: Average daily water demand in Million Gallons per Day (MGD) for the pressure zone, used for capacity planning and hydraulic modeling. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: average_elevation_ft
attributes.description: Average ground elevation in feet above sea level across the pressure zone, used for hydraulic modeling and demand allocation. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: boundary_description
attributes.description: Textual description of the geographic or infrastructure boundaries defining the pressure zone, including major streets, landmarks, or infrastructure features. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: commissioning_date
attributes.description: Date when the pressure zone was officially commissioned and placed into active service for water distribution operations. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this pressure zone record was first created in the system, used for audit trail and data lineage tracking. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: customer_count
attributes.description: Total number of active customer service connections within the pressure zone, used for demand forecasting and revenue allocation. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: design_pressure_psi
attributes.description: Design or nominal operating pressure in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI) for which the zone infrastructure was engineered and constructed. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: elevation_max_ft
attributes.description: Maximum ground elevation in feet above sea level within the pressure zone boundary, critical for pressure management and PRV settings. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: elevation_min_ft
attributes.description: Minimum ground elevation in feet above sea level within the pressure zone boundary, used for hydraulic gradient calculations. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: fire_flow_capacity_gpm
attributes.description: Minimum fire flow capacity in Gallons per Minute (GPM) that the pressure zone must maintain at specified residual pressure for fire protection, per Insurance Services Office (ISO) and NFPA standards.

attributes.name: hydraulic_model_last_calibrated_date
attributes.description: Date when the hydraulic model for this pressure zone was last calibrated against field measurements, ensuring model accuracy for planning and operational decisions. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: infowater_model_zone_code
attributes.description: Corresponding pressure zone identifier in the Innovyze InfoWater hydraulic model, used for synchronization between operational systems and modeling platforms. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: last_boundary_review_date
attributes.description: Date when the pressure zone boundaries were last reviewed and validated for accuracy, typically as part of GIS updates or hydraulic model recalibration. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this pressure zone record was last modified, used for audit trail, change tracking, and data synchronization. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: mutator_note
attributes.description: The mutator note value recorded for each pressure zone in the distribution domain.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special considerations, historical context, or other relevant information about the pressure zone. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: nrw_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of Non-Revenue Water (NRW) within the pressure zone, calculated as the difference between water supplied and billed consumption, used for loss control and efficiency analysis. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational state of the pressure zone indicating whether it is actively serving customers, temporarily inactive, under maintenance, in emergency mode, or in planned development. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: peak_hour_demand_mgd
attributes.description: Peak hourly water demand in Million Gallons per Day (MGD) for the pressure zone, critical for sizing infrastructure and ensuring adequate pressure during high-demand periods. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: residual_pressure_fire_psi
attributes.description: Minimum residual pressure in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI) that must be maintained during fire flow conditions to ensure adequate service to other customers and fire suppression effectiveness. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: scada_zone_tag

attributes.description: SCADA system tag or point identifier for real-time monitoring of pressure, flow, and operational status within this zone via OSIsoft PI Historian or similar SCADA platforms.

attributes.name: service_area_sq_mi

attributes.name: storage_capacity_mg

attributes.name: target_pressure_max_psi
attributes.description: Maximum target operating pressure in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI) to prevent infrastructure damage, excessive leakage, and customer service issues. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: target_pressure_min_psi
attributes.description: Minimum target operating pressure in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI) that must be maintained throughout the zone to ensure adequate service delivery and regulatory compliance. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: ufw_percentage

attributes.name: zone_code

attributes.name: zone_name

attributes.name: zone_type

products.name: dma
products.description: District Metered Areas (DMAs) for water loss control and non-revenue water (NRW) management. Each DMA is a discrete zone with defined boundaries, inlet/outlet metering, and isolation valves enabling water balance calculations per IWA Water Loss Task Force methodology. Tracks minimum night flow, leakage detection frequency, infrastructure leakage index (ILI), and target NRW percentages. Central to AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs.
products.reference: AWWA M36, IWA Water Loss Task Force, ISO 4064 Water Meters

attributes.name: pressure_zone_id

attributes.name: average_pressure_psi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Average Pressure in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI)
attributes.description: Average operating pressure within the DMA measured in Pounds per Square Inch. Pressure management is critical for leakage control; excessive pressure increases leak rates and pipe stress. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.description: Business criticality rating of the DMA based on factors such as population served, infrastructure condition, leakage history, and service area importance. Critical DMAs receive priority for monitoring and maintenance. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: description

attributes.name: design_flow_mgd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Design Flow in Million Gallons per Day (MGD)
attributes.description: Design flow capacity for the DMA in Million Gallons per Day. Represents the maximum daily demand the DMA is engineered to supply under normal operating conditions. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: dma_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the DMA. Active DMAs are fully operational and monitored; inactive or decommissioned DMAs are no longer in use; planned DMAs are in design phase; under review indicates reconfiguration or audit in progress. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: established_date
attributes.description: Date when the DMA was first established and commissioned for operational monitoring. Represents the start of the DMAs lifecycle. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: gis_polygon_boundary
attributes.description: GIS polygon geometry defining the spatial boundary of the DMA. Typically stored as WKT (Well-Known Text) or reference to GIS layer feature ID for integration with Esri ArcGIS. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: inlet_meter_count
attributes.description: Number of inlet flow meters installed at entry points to the DMA. Inlet meters measure total water entering the zone and are critical for NRW calculation. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: isolation_valve_count
attributes.description: Number of isolation valves installed at the DMA boundary. Isolation valves enable hydraulic isolation of the DMA for accurate flow measurement and leakage detection.

attributes.name: last_leakage_survey_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent active leakage detection survey conducted within the DMA. Used to track compliance with leakage management programs. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp

attributes.name: leakage_detection_frequency_days
attributes.description: Frequency in days at which active leakage detection surveys are conducted within the DMA. High-risk or high-leakage DMAs may be surveyed more frequently. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: main_length_miles
attributes.description: Total length of water mains (distribution pipes) within the DMA measured in miles. Used for calculating leakage per mile of main and infrastructure density metrics. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: minimum_night_flow_threshold_gpm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Minimum Night Flow (MNF) Threshold in Gallons per Minute (GPM)
attributes.description: Minimum Night Flow threshold in Gallons per Minute. MNF is the lowest flow rate measured during nighttime hours (typically 2 AM to 4 AM) when legitimate consumption is minimal. Elevated MNF indicates leakage within the DMA. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

tag_set.value: Minimum Night Flow (MNF) Threshold in Gallons per Minute (GPM)

attributes.name: mutator_note
attributes.description: The mutator note value recorded for each dma in the distribution domain.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or designation of the DMA, often reflecting geographic location or service area (e.g., 'Downtown West DMA', 'Industrial Park Zone 3'). Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: next_scheduled_survey_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next active leakage detection survey within the DMA. Used for planning and resource allocation. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special instructions, historical context, or any additional information relevant to the DMA management and monitoring. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: outlet_meter_count
attributes.description: Number of outlet flow meters installed at exit points from the DMA. Outlet meters are used in complex DMA configurations where water may flow to adjacent zones. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: population_served
attributes.description: Estimated population served by the DMA. Used for per-capita consumption analysis and demand forecasting. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: prv_count
attributes.description: Number of Pressure Reducing Valves installed within or at the boundary of the DMA. PRVs control pressure to reduce leakage and pipe stress. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: scada_monitored_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Monitored Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DMA is actively monitored by the SCADA system. SCADA-monitored DMAs provide real-time flow, pressure, and alarm data for proactive leakage management. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

tag_set.value: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Monitored Flag

attributes.name: service_connection_count
attributes.description: Total number of active service connections (customer meters) within the DMA. Used for calculating per-connection leakage rates and NRW metrics. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: target_nrw_percentage
attributes.description: Target threshold for Non-Revenue Water as a percentage of total water supplied to the DMA. NRW includes physical losses (leakage) and commercial losses (metering inaccuracies, theft). Typical industry targets range from 10% to 20%. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: target_ufw_percentage
attributes.description: Target threshold for Unaccounted-for Water as a percentage of total water supplied. UFW is a broader measure than NRW and includes all water that cannot be accounted for through billing or authorized use. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

products.name: network_valve
products.description: Isolation and control valves in the distribution network. Tracks valve type (gate, butterfly, ball), size, material, position, exercising history, and operability status. Regular valve exercising programs per AWWA M44 Distribution Valves prevent valve failures during emergencies. Links to asset registry, work orders, and maintenance schedules in IBM Maximo.
products.reference: AWWA M44 Distribution Valves, AWWA C500 Gate Valves, AWWA C504 Butterfly Valves

attributes.name: network_valve_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the distribution network valve record. Primary key. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: dma_id
attributes.description: Reference to the District Metered Area (DMA) containing this valve. DMAs are isolated network sections with defined boundaries and metered inflows/outflows, used for Non-Revenue Water (NRW) and Unaccounted-for Water (UFW) analysis. Valves on DMA boundaries are critical for isolation and flow control.

attributes.name: network_registry_id
attributes.description: Reference to the asset registry record in the Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS). Links this valve to IBM Maximo Asset Management for maintenance tracking, work orders, and lifecycle management.

attributes.name: pipe_main_id
attributes.description: Reference to the water main on which this valve is installed. Links the valve to the pipe segment for network topology modeling in Esri ArcGIS and Innovyze InfoWater. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: pm_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.pm_schedule. Business justification: AWWA M44 and regulatory standards require periodic valve exercising programs. network_valve has exercising_frequency_months as a plain attribute but no link to the formal PM schedule that drives work

attributes.name: pressure_zone_id
attributes.description: Reference to the pressure zone in which this valve is located. Pressure zones are geographic areas maintained at specific pressure ranges (measured in Pounds per Square Inch - PSI) to ensure adequate service and prevent pipe bursts. Critical for hydraulic modeling in Innovyze InfoWater. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: burial_depth_feet
attributes.description: Depth in feet from ground surface to the valve operating nut. Used for excavation planning, valve box sizing, and accessibility assessment. Typical range is 3-8 feet depending on frost line and main depth. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: city
attributes.description: City or municipality in which the valve is located. Used for jurisdictional reporting and geographic analysis. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: condition_rating
attributes.description: Assessment of the valve's physical condition based on the most recent inspection. Excellent: like new, no defects; Good: minor wear, fully functional; Fair: moderate wear, functional with minor issues; Poor: significant deterioration, may fail soon; Critical: immediate replacement required. Used for risk-based asset management and Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) planning. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this valve record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage, audit trails, and compliance with data governance policies. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: criticality_rating
attributes.description: Business criticality of the valve based on its role in the distribution network. Critical valves control large trunk mains or serve hospitals/fire protection; high criticality valves isolate major zones; medium and low criticality valves serve smaller areas. Drives maintenance prioritization and replacement sequencing.

attributes.name: current_position
attributes.description: Actual current position of the valve as of the last field verification or SCADA reading. May differ from normal_position during maintenance, emergencies, or operational adjustments. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: diameter_inches
attributes.description: Nominal diameter of the valve in inches. Critical for hydraulic modeling in Innovyze InfoWater and flow capacity calculations. Common sizes range from 2 to 48 inches in distribution networks. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: exercising_frequency_months
attributes.description: Planned frequency in months for valve exercising activities. Typically 12 months for standard valves, 6 months for critical isolation valves, and 24 months for low-priority valves. Drives preventive maintenance scheduling in CMMS.

attributes.name: gis_feature_code
attributes.description: Unique feature identifier in the Esri ArcGIS system. Links this valve record to the corresponding GIS feature layer for spatial analysis, map display, and network topology modeling. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date the valve was originally installed in the distribution network. Used for age-based asset management, depreciation calculations, and replacement planning under the Capital Improvement Program (CIP). Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: installation_year
attributes.description: Year the valve was installed. Derived from installation_date for simplified age analysis and reporting when exact date is not required. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: is_buried
attributes.description: Indicates whether the valve is buried underground (True) or above ground in a vault or building (False). Buried valves require valve box access and are more difficult to exercise; above-ground valves are more accessible but require weather protection. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: is_motorized
attributes.description: Indicates whether the valve is equipped with a motor or actuator for remote operation. True for SCADA-controlled valves; False for manual valves requiring field crew operation. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: last_exercised_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the crew member or contractor who last exercised the valve. Supports accountability and quality assurance in valve maintenance programs. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: last_exercised_date
attributes.description: Date the valve was last exercised (opened and closed through its full range of motion). Regular valve exercising prevents seizing and ensures operability during emergencies. AWWA recommends annual exercising for critical valves.

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the valve location in decimal degrees. Used for Geographic Information System (GIS) mapping in Esri ArcGIS, field crew navigation, and spatial analysis. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the valve location in decimal degrees. Used for Geographic Information System (GIS) mapping in Esri ArcGIS, field crew navigation, and spatial analysis. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: material
attributes.description: Primary construction material of the valve body. Ductile iron is most common for large distribution valves; bronze and brass for smaller service valves; stainless steel for corrosive environments; PVC for low-pressure applications. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this valve record was last modified. Supports change tracking, audit requirements, and data quality monitoring. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: mutator_note
attributes.description: The mutator note value recorded for each network valve in the distribution domain.

attributes.name: normal_position
attributes.description: Standard operating position of the valve under normal conditions. Critical for hydraulic modeling, isolation planning, and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) monitoring. Most distribution valves are normally open; some isolation and control valves are normally closed or throttled.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, special instructions, access restrictions, or historical information about the valve. Examples: 'Requires two-person crew due to tight turns', 'Located in private easement, coordinate access', 'Replaced stem in 2018'. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: operating_pressure_psi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Valve Operating Pressure (Pounds per Square Inch - PSI)
attributes.description: Normal operating pressure at the valve location in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI). Used for hydraulic modeling, pressure zone verification, and valve sizing validation. Typical distribution system pressures range from 40-120 PSI. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

tag_set.value: Valve Operating Pressure (Pounds per Square Inch - PSI)

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the valve in the distribution network. Active valves are in service; inactive valves are temporarily out of service; abandoned valves are no longer used but not removed; removed valves have been physically extracted; planned valves are scheduled for installation. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: postal_code
attributes.description: Postal code of the valve location. Supports geographic segmentation and service area analysis. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: pressure_rating_psi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Valve Pressure Rating (Pounds per Square Inch - PSI)
attributes.description: Maximum rated working pressure of the valve in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI) as specified by the manufacturer. Must exceed operating_pressure_psi with adequate safety margin. Common ratings are 150, 200, 250, and 300 PSI. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

tag_set.value: Valve Pressure Rating (Pounds per Square Inch - PSI)

attributes.name: scada_tag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Tag
attributes.description: SCADA system tag identifier for automated valves with remote monitoring and control capability. Links to OSIsoft PI Historian for real-time position monitoring, alarm management, and operational analytics. Only populated for motorized or actuated valves integrated with SCADA.

tag_set.value: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Tag

attributes.name: state_province
attributes.description: State or province in which the valve is located. Used for regulatory reporting to State Drinking Water Programs and Primacy Agencies. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: street_address
attributes.description: Nearest street address or intersection to the valve location. Provides human-readable location reference for field crews, emergency responders, and customer service representatives. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: turns_to_close
attributes.description: Number of complete turns required to fully close the valve from the fully open position. Used by field crews during valve exercising programs and emergency isolation procedures. Typical range is 5-50 turns depending on valve size and type.

attributes.name: useful_life_years
attributes.description: Expected useful life of the valve in years from installation date. Used for depreciation calculations per Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB) standards, and for long-term replacement planning. Typical range is 50-75 years for distribution valves. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: valve_box_type
attributes.description: Type of valve box or access structure protecting the buried valve. Standard boxes for sidewalk/lawn areas; traffic-rated boxes for roadways; extension boxes for deep valves; vaults for large valves; none for above-ground installations. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: valve_function
attributes.description: Primary operational function of the valve in the distribution network. Isolation valves segment the network for maintenance; control valves regulate flow; pressure reducing valves (PRV) manage pressure zones; check valves prevent backflow; air release valves expel trapped air; blowoff valves drain sections.

attributes.name: valve_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the valve, typically painted or tagged on the valve in the field. Used by operations and maintenance crews for identification. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: valve_type
attributes.description: Classification of the valve mechanism. Gate valves provide full flow with minimal pressure drop; butterfly valves are compact and quick-operating; ball valves offer tight shutoff; check valves prevent backflow; plug, cone, and needle valves provide throttling control. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: gate|butterfly|ball|check|plug|cone|needle — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

products.name: hydrant
products.description: Fire hydrants providing emergency water supply for fire protection. Tracks hydrant type, outlet configuration, flow capacity, static/residual pressures, flow test results, flushing history, and NFPA color classification. Flow testing per AWWA M17 Installation, Field Testing, and Maintenance of Fire Hydrants supports ISO fire flow ratings and hydraulic model calibration.
products.reference: AWWA M17, AWWA C502 Dry-Barrel Fire Hydrants, NFPA 291 Fire Flow Testing, ISO Fire Suppression Rating Schedule

attributes.name: hydrant_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the fire hydrant asset in the distribution network. Primary key. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: dma_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the District Metered Area (DMA) to which the hydrant belongs, used for Non-Revenue Water (NRW) analysis and leak detection programs. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: hydrant_main_pipe_pipe_main_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the nearest or connected water main pipe from which the hydrant is fed, used for hydraulic modeling and network topology analysis. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: hydrant_pipe_main_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the nearest or connected water main pipe from which the hydrant is fed, used for hydraulic modeling and network topology analysis. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: pm_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.pm_schedule. Business justification: NFPA 291 and ISO 9001 require annual hydrant flow testing and flushing programs. hydrant has flushing_program_flag and last_flushing_date as plain attributes but no link to the formal PM schedule. Thi

attributes.name: pressure_zone_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the pressure zone or hydraulic district in which the hydrant is located, used for pressure management and network segmentation. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: bury_depth_feet
attributes.description: Depth in feet from ground surface to the hydrant valve or base, critical for freeze protection and installation specifications. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: city
attributes.description: City or municipality name where the hydrant is located. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: condition_status
attributes.description: Current physical condition assessment of the hydrant based on inspection findings: excellent (like new), good (minor wear), fair (functional with moderate wear), poor (requires repair), critical (non-functional or unsafe). Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this hydrant record was first created in the asset management system. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: criticality_rating
attributes.description: Business criticality rating based on consequence-of-failure analysis: critical (hospitals, schools, high-density areas), high (commercial districts), medium (residential), low (rural or redundant coverage). Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: fire_district
attributes.description: Name or code of the fire protection district or fire department jurisdiction responsible for this hydrant, used for emergency response coordination. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: flow_capacity_gpm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Fire Flow Capacity in Gallons Per Minute (GPM)
attributes.description: Rated fire flow capacity of the hydrant in gallons per minute (GPM) at 20 pounds per square inch (PSI) residual pressure, determined by flow testing per NFPA 291. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

tag_set.value: Fire Flow Capacity in Gallons Per Minute (GPM)

attributes.name: flow_class_color
attributes.business_glossary_term: National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) Flow Class Color Code
attributes.description: Color coding per NFPA 291 indicating fire flow capacity class: Red (<500 GPM), Orange (500-999 GPM), Green (1000-1499 GPM), Blue (>=1500 GPM), Light Blue (>=2500 GPM). Used for visual identification by fire departments. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

tag_set.value: National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) Flow Class Color Code

attributes.name: flushing_program_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this hydrant is included in the routine unidirectional flushing program for water quality maintenance and sediment removal. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: gis_feature_code
attributes.description: Unique feature identifier from the Esri ArcGIS system linking this hydrant record to the spatial GIS layer for network modeling and map visualization. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: hydrant_number
attributes.description: External business identifier or asset tag number assigned to the hydrant for field operations, maintenance tracking, and municipal records. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: hydrant_type
attributes.description: Classification of hydrant design. Dry barrel hydrants drain after use (freeze-resistant for cold climates), wet barrel hydrants remain charged with water (warm climates), flush hydrants are below-grade, wall hydrants are building-mounted. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date when the hydrant was originally installed in the distribution network. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: installation_year
attributes.description: Year of hydrant installation, used for age-based asset management, depreciation schedules, and replacement planning. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: last_flow_test_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent fire flow test conducted on the hydrant per NFPA 291 standards, used to verify flow capacity and pressure performance. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: last_flushing_date
attributes.description: Date when the hydrant was last used for system flushing or water quality maintenance activities. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent routine inspection of the hydrant for physical condition, operability, and maintenance needs. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this hydrant record was last updated in the asset management system, used for audit trail and data lineage tracking. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate (WGS84 decimal degrees) of the hydrant location for GIS mapping, spatial analysis, and emergency response routing. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate (WGS84 decimal degrees) of the hydrant location for GIS mapping, spatial analysis, and emergency response routing. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: main_diameter_inches
attributes.description: Diameter of the connected water main pipe in inches, critical for fire flow capacity calculations and hydraulic modeling. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: mutator_note
attributes.description: The mutator note value recorded for each hydrant in the distribution domain.

attributes.name: next_inspection_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next routine inspection of the hydrant, based on preventive maintenance (PM) schedule and regulatory requirements. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, observations, or special instructions related to the hydrant (e.g., access restrictions, historical issues, special maintenance requirements). Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the hydrant in the distribution network: in_service (active and available), out_of_service (temporarily unavailable), under_repair (maintenance in progress), abandoned (permanently removed from service), planned (not yet installed). Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: outlet_count
attributes.description: Total number of discharge outlets (nozzles) on the hydrant, typically 2-5 outlets including pumper and hose connections. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: outlet_size_inches
attributes.description: Sizes of hydrant outlets in inches, typically formatted as a comma-separated list (e.g., '2.5,2.5,4.5' for two 2.5-inch hose outlets and one 4.5-inch pumper outlet). Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: ownership_type
attributes.description: Entity responsible for ownership and maintenance of the hydrant: utility_owned (water utility), municipality_owned (city/town), private (property owner), fire_district (fire protection district). Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: postal_code
attributes.description: Postal or ZIP code for the hydrant location, used for geographic segmentation and service area analysis. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: residual_pressure_psi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Residual Pressure in Pounds Per Square Inch (PSI)
attributes.description: Residual water pressure at the hydrant in pounds per square inch (PSI) during flow testing at rated capacity, used to assess available fire flow. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

tag_set.value: Residual Pressure in Pounds Per Square Inch (PSI)

attributes.name: scada_tag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Tag Identifier
attributes.description: SCADA system tag or point identifier if the hydrant is equipped with remote monitoring sensors (e.g., pressure transducers), integrated with OSIsoft PI Historian.

tag_set.value: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Tag Identifier

attributes.name: state_province
attributes.description: State or province code (e.g., CA, TX, ON) where the hydrant is located. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: static_pressure_psi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Static Pressure in Pounds Per Square Inch (PSI)
attributes.description: Static water pressure at the hydrant location in pounds per square inch (PSI) when no water is flowing, measured during flow testing. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

tag_set.value: Static Pressure in Pounds Per Square Inch (PSI)

attributes.name: street_address
attributes.description: Street address or nearest intersection where the hydrant is located, used for field crew dispatch and fire department coordination. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

attributes.name: valve_turns_to_open
attributes.business_glossary_term: Valve Turns Required to Fully Open
attributes.description: Number of complete turns required to fully open the hydrant main valve, used for operational training and maintenance documentation. Ref: OSIsoft PI Historian.

tag_set.value: Valve Turns Required to Fully Open

Energy monitoring supports efficiency optimization per AWWA M32. Links to asset registry, work orders, and energy meters.
products.reference: AWWA M32, AWWA M11, Hydraulic Institute Standards, ISO 24516-1:2016

Compliance managers track permit coverage per pump station for regulat

attributes.name: dma_id

attributes.name: pressure_zone_id

attributes.name: asset_condition_rating

attributes.name: backup_generator_available

attributes.name: backup_generator_capacity_kw

attributes.name: country_code

attributes.name: design_flow_capacity_gpm

attributes.name: mutator_note

domains.name: billing
domains.description: Revenue cycle management including consumption-based billing, rate structures, invoice generation, payment processing, payment plans, collections, delinquency management, billing adjustments, dispute resolution, and revenue recognition. SSOT for all financial transactions with customers including water, wastewater, stormwater, and other utility charges.

products.name: invoice
products.description: Core billing document representing a periodic, on-demand, or final statement of charges issued to a customer billing account for water, wastewater, stormwater, and other utility services. Captures billing period, due date, total amount due, invoice status (draft, issued, paid, overdue, cancelled), bill type (regular cycle, final, estimated, corrected, off-cycle), generation method, closing meter read reference (for final bills), deposit application amount, and forwarding address (for final bill refunds). SSOT for all customer-facing billing documents including final bills upon service termination.

attributes.name: conservation_message
attributes.description: Optional water conservation message or tip printed on the invoice to encourage efficient water use. May vary seasonally or based on drought conditions. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.description: User ID or system process name that created this invoice record. For automated cycle billing, typically a batch process identifier; for manual invoices, the billing staff user ID. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this invoice record was first created in the billing system. Used for audit trail and data lineage. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts on this invoice. Typically USD for U.S. water utilities.

attributes.name: delivery_method
attributes.description: Method by which the invoice was delivered to the customer. Options include postal mail (paper bill), email (electronic bill), customer web portal, or SMS notification with portal link. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: disconnection_date
attributes.description: Date on which service may be disconnected if payment is not received. Typically set 10-15 days after due date, subject to regulatory notice requirements and customer protections. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: dispute_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the customer has formally disputed charges on this invoice. Triggers dispute resolution workflow and may suspend collection activities. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: due_date
attributes.description: Date by which payment must be received to avoid late fees or service disconnection. Calculated based on invoice date plus payment terms (typically 15-30 days). Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: generation_method
attributes.description: Method by which the invoice was generated. Automated cycle invoices are produced by scheduled batch billing runs; manual invoices are created by billing staff; off-cycle invoices are generated outside normal schedules; estimated invoices use projected consumption; corrected invoices replace prior errors. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: invoice_date
attributes.description: Date the invoice was generated and issued to the customer. This is the official invoice date printed on the bill and used for aging calculations. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: invoice_number
attributes.description: Externally visible, human-readable invoice number printed on customer bills and used for customer service inquiries. Must be unique across all invoices. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: invoice_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the invoice. Draft invoices are pending finalization; issued invoices have been sent to customers; paid invoices are fully settled; partial_paid invoices have received some payment; overdue invoices are past due date; cancelled invoices are nullified before payment; void invoices are nullified after issuance. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|issued|paid|partial_paid|overdue|cancelled|void — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: invoice_type
attributes.description: Classification of the invoice based on billing circumstances. Regular cycle invoices are standard periodic bills; final invoices are issued upon service termination; estimated invoices use projected consumption when actual reads are unavailable; corrected invoices replace erroneous prior bills; off-cycle invoices are generated outside normal billing cycles; adjustment invoices correct prior billing errors. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: is_estimated

attributes.name: is_final

attributes.name: late_fee_amount

attributes.name: period_start_date

attributes.name: print_date

attributes.name: stormwater_area
attributes.description: Total impervious surface area (in square feet or square meters) used to calculate stormwater management fees. Applicable for properties subject to stormwater utility charges. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.description: Charges for stormwater management services, typically calculated based on impervious surface area. Supports stormwater infrastructure maintenance and regulatory compliance. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: tax_amount

attributes.name: total_amount_due

attributes.name: total_amount_usd

attributes.name: wastewater_volume

attributes.name: water_charge_amount

attributes.name: water_consumption_uom
attributes.description: Unit of measure for water consumption volume. Common units include gallons, cubic meters (m³), hundred cubic feet (CCF), or thousand gallons (kgal). Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: water_consumption_volume
attributes.description: Total volume of potable water consumed during the billing period, measured in gallons or cubic meters depending on utility standard. Derived from meter readings or estimated when actual reads unavailable. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

products.name: invoice_line

SSOT for all individual charges appearing on customer invoices.

attributes.description: Custom calculation expression for formula-based components. Contains the algorithmic logic used to compute the charge amount, referencing other rate components, usage data, or account attributes. Null for standard calculation methods. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: calculation_method
attributes.description: Algorithm used to calculate the charge amount. Flat amount applies a fixed charge regardless of usage, per-unit multiplies usage by unit rate, tiered block applies different rates to usage ranges, percentage applies a rate to another charge, and formula uses a custom calculation expression. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: component_code
attributes.description: Business identifier code for the rate component used in billing systems and rate books. Examples: BASE_CHG, TIER1_VOL, DEMAND_CHG, STORMWATER_FEE. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: component_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the rate component. Examples: Base Service Charge, First Tier Volumetric Charge, Peak Demand Charge, Stormwater Management Fee. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: component_type
attributes.description: Classification of the rate component defining its billing purpose. Base charges are fixed monthly fees, volumetric charges are consumption-based, demand charges are based on peak usage, tier charges apply to usage blocks, surcharges are additional fees, taxes are regulatory levies, fees are service-specific charges, adjustments modify base amounts, and credits reduce charges. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: base_charge|volumetric_charge|demand_charge|tier_charge|surcharge|tax|fee|adjustment|credit — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: conservation_tier_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this component is part of a conservation-oriented inclining block rate structure designed to discourage excessive water use. True for higher-tier volumetric charges that increase with consumption. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: cost_center
attributes.description: Cost center code for internal cost allocation and profitability analysis. Links revenue to the organizational unit or service line responsible for the charge. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the rate component record was first created in the system. Used for audit trails and data lineage tracking. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Detailed business description of the rate component, its purpose, and how it is applied. Provides context for billing staff, customer service representatives, and customers reviewing their bills. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The effective date associated with each rate component record in the billing domain.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date when this rate component ceases to be active. Null indicates the component is currently active with no planned end date. Used for rate schedule versioning and historical rate reconstruction. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when this rate component becomes active and applicable to billing. Supports rate change management and regulatory compliance with rate case approval timelines. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: The expiration date associated with each rate component record in the billing domain.

attributes.name: flat_amount
attributes.description: Fixed charge amount for flat-rate components such as base service charges, connection fees, or fixed surcharges. Null for volumetric or percentage-based components. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: gl_account_code
attributes.description: General ledger account code to which revenue from this component is posted. Links billing transactions to the financial accounting system for revenue recognition and reporting. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: is_prorated
attributes.description: Indicates whether the component should be prorated for partial billing periods. True if the charge should be adjusted proportionally when service starts or ends mid-cycle. False if the full charge applies regardless of billing period length. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: is_taxable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this component is subject to sales tax or other tax levies. True if the component amount should be included in the taxable base for tax calculation. False if exempt from taxation. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: is_volumetric
attributes.description: Indicates whether the component is consumption-based (volumetric) or fixed. True for components that vary with usage (per-unit, tiered block). False for fixed charges (base charges, flat fees). Used to distinguish variable from fixed revenue components. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the rate component record was last updated. Used for change tracking and audit compliance. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: meter_size_applicability
attributes.description: Meter size or size range to which this component applies. Used for meter-size-based base charges. Examples: 5/8 inch, 1 inch, 2 inch, 3 inch and larger. Null if component applies to all meter sizes. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: percentage_rate
attributes.description: Percentage rate applied for percentage-based components such as taxes, surcharges, or adjustments. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0825 for 8.25% sales tax). Null for non-percentage components. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: print_on_bill_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this component should be displayed as a separate line item on customer bills. True for components that require transparency and customer visibility. False for internal calculation components. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: rate_case_number
attributes.description: Regulatory rate case docket number or internal rate change request identifier associated with this component. Links the component to the formal rate approval process. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: rate_component_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the rate component. Active components are in use for billing. Inactive components are temporarily disabled. Ref: Oracle CC&B.

attributes.name: rate_usd

attributes.name: regulatory_reporting_category

attributes.name: revenue_class

attributes.name: seasonal_indicator

attributes.name: tier_high_threshold

attributes.name: tier_low_threshold

products.name: payment_plan
products.description: Structured payment arrangement for customers, covering delinquent balance repayment plans, budget billing (levelized payment) programs, and utility assistance installment plans. For deferred payment agreements: captures enrolled delinquent balance, installment amount/frequency, plan status, and break conditions. For budget billing: captures monthly budget amount, true-up month, cumulative actual vs billed variance, and annual reconciliation. Supports LIHEAP coordination, low-income assistance plans, and service disconnection avoidance. SSOT for all structured payment arrangements on a billing account.

domains.name: wastewater
domains.description: Manages wastewater collection, conveyance, and treatment operations including sewer network topology, gravity sewers, force mains, lift stations, manholes, CSO/SSO management, I&I monitoring, FOG program management, industrial user permits (IUP), and NPDES compliance tracking. Supports DMR submissions and biosolids management.

products.name: sewer_network
products.description: Master topology of the wastewater collection and conveyance network including gravity sewers, force mains, interceptors, and trunk lines. Captures pipe material, diameter, length, slope, invert elevations, installation year, condition grade, and GIS geometry. Each segment is individually identifiable by upstream/downstream manhole nodes. Serves as the authoritative spatial and hydraulic reference for the sewer system, aligned with Esri ArcGIS Utility Network and Innovyze InfoSWMM/ICM hydraulic models.
products.reference: Cited standards & systems of record: AWWA; EPA SDWA

attributes.name: sewer_network_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the sewer network segment. Primary key for the sewer network master topology. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.business_glossary_term: NPDES (National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System) Permit ID
attributes.description: National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit identifier if this segment is subject to specific discharge monitoring or CSO/SSO reporting requirements. Ref: EPA SDWA.

tag_set.value: NPDES (National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System) Permit ID

attributes.name: wwtp_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) that receives flow from this sewer segment. Supports load allocation and treatment capacity planning. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: asset_tag
attributes.description: Physical asset tag or barcode identifier affixed to the segment or associated manhole for field identification and work order tracking in IBM Maximo.

attributes.name: average_daily_flow_mgd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Average Daily Flow (MGD - Million Gallons per Day)
attributes.description: Average daily wastewater flow through the segment in Million Gallons per Day (MGD). Used for load balancing and treatment plant influent forecasting. Ref: EPA SDWA.

tag_set.value: Average Daily Flow (MGD - Million Gallons per Day)

attributes.name: condition_grade
attributes.description: Current physical condition assessment of the sewer segment based on CCTV inspection, PACP (Pipeline Assessment and Certification Program) scoring, or field evaluation. Drives maintenance and replacement decisions. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: coordinate_system
attributes.description: Spatial reference system identifier (e.g., EPSG code) for the GIS geometry. Ensures spatial data interoperability and accurate georeferencing. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this sewer network record was first created in the system. Supports data lineage and audit trail requirements. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: criticality_score
attributes.description: Risk-based criticality rating (typically 1-100 scale) reflecting consequence of failure, service impact, and environmental risk. Drives capital investment prioritization. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Identifier of the source system or data collection method that provided this record (e.g., Esri ArcGIS, field survey, as-built drawings, CCTV inspection). Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: design_capacity_mgd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Design Capacity (MGD - Million Gallons per Day)
attributes.description: Hydraulic design capacity of the sewer segment in Million Gallons per Day (MGD). Used for capacity utilization analysis and growth planning. Ref: EPA SDWA.

tag_set.value: Design Capacity (MGD - Million Gallons per Day)

attributes.name: diameter_inches
attributes.description: Internal diameter of the sewer pipe in inches. Key hydraulic parameter for capacity analysis and flow modeling in Innovyze InfoWater. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: downstream_invert_elevation_feet
attributes.description: Elevation of the inside bottom of the pipe at the downstream end in feet above mean sea level. Used with upstream invert to calculate slope and hydraulic capacity. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: easement_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a legal easement is required for utility access to the sewer segment. Critical for maintenance planning and right-of-way management. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: fog_risk_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: FOG (Fats Oils and Grease) Risk Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the segment is at elevated risk for FOG (Fats, Oils, and Grease) blockages based on upstream land use (restaurants, food processing). Drives preventive maintenance frequency. Ref: EPA SDWA.

tag_set.value: FOG (Fats Oils and Grease) Risk Flag

attributes.description: Auto‑generated attribute for sewer_network. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: gis_geometry_wkt
attributes.description: Well-Known Text (WKT) representation of the sewer segment spatial geometry (typically LINESTRING). Authoritative spatial reference for GIS mapping and network analysis in Esri ArcGIS. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: hydrogen_sulfide_risk_flag
attributes.description: Indicates elevated risk of hydrogen sulfide gas generation and corrosion. Common in force mains and long gravity sewers with low flow velocity. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: installation_year
attributes.description: Year the sewer segment was originally installed. Key attribute for asset age analysis, depreciation schedules, and capital improvement program (CIP) prioritization. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent CCTV or physical inspection of the sewer segment. Supports compliance with regulatory inspection frequency requirements and condition assessment programs. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this sewer network record. Enables change tracking and data quality monitoring. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: length_feet
attributes.description: Physical length of the sewer segment in feet measured from upstream to downstream node. Used for asset inventory valuation and hydraulic calculations. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: lining_installation_date
attributes.description: Date when pipe lining or rehabilitation was completed. Resets the effective age for condition assessment and extends asset useful life. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: lining_type
attributes.description: Type of trenchless rehabilitation lining applied to the sewer segment. CIPP (Cured-in-Place Pipe) is a common method for structural renewal without excavation. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: next_inspection_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next required inspection based on regulatory mandates, risk-based prioritization, or preventive maintenance cycles. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special conditions, historical context, or field observations relevant to the sewer segment. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the sewer segment in the collection network. Active segments are in service; abandoned segments are out of service but not removed. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: ownership_type
attributes.description: Legal ownership classification of the sewer segment. Determines maintenance responsibility, regulatory jurisdiction, and capital funding eligibility. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: peak_flow_gpm
attributes.description: Maximum observed or modeled flow rate in Gallons per Minute (GPM) during peak wet weather or high demand periods. Critical for SSO risk assessment. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: replacement_cost_usd
attributes.description: Estimated current replacement cost of the sewer segment in US Dollars. Used for asset valuation, insurance, and capital improvement program (CIP) budgeting. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: root_intrusion_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether tree root intrusion has been observed or is a known risk for this segment. Common in older vitrified clay and concrete pipes. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: segment_identifier
attributes.description: Externally-known unique identifier for the sewer segment used in GIS systems, field operations, and regulatory reporting. Aligns with Esri ArcGIS feature identifiers. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: segment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the sewer segment by conveyance method and network hierarchy. Gravity sewers use slope for flow; force mains use pumps; interceptors and trunk lines are major collectors. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: slope_percent
attributes.description: Gradient of the sewer pipe expressed as a percentage. Critical for gravity sewer hydraulic performance and self-cleansing velocity calculations. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: sso_history_count
attributes.description: Number of Sanitary Sewer Overflow (SSO) events recorded for this segment. High counts trigger regulatory scrutiny and prioritize capacity upgrades. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: traffic_impact_level
attributes.description: Assessment of traffic disruption risk if the segment requires excavation or repair. High-traffic segments require special permitting and coordination. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Record last update timestamp. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: upstream_invert_elevation_feet
attributes.description: Elevation of the inside bottom of the pipe at the upstream end in feet above mean sea level. Essential for hydraulic grade line analysis and I&I (Inflow and Infiltration) assessment. Ref: EPA SDWA.

products.name: manhole
products.description: Master record for each manhole structure in the wastewater collection system including rim elevation, invert elevation, depth, material, cover type, condition rating, GIS coordinates, and inspection status. Manholes are key access and junction points in the gravity sewer network and are individually tracked for maintenance and I&I assessment.

attributes.description: Internal diameter of the manhole structure measured in inches. Standard diameters are 48 inches (4 feet) or 60 inches (5 feet) for personnel access. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: dma_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the District Metered Area (DMA) or pressure zone to which this manhole belongs. Used for network segmentation and performance monitoring. Ref: EPA SDWA.

products.name: sewer_service_connection
products.description: Master record for each individual sewer service connection (lateral) linking a customer premise to the public sewer main including connection address, parcel identifier, lateral pipe material, diameter, length, connection type (gravity, grinder pump), installation date, condition, and service status (active, inactive, abandoned). Bridges the wastewater network topology to customer service accounts.
